title: Affine case of the single-complex derived base-change criterion
statement: Let X=Spec(A), S=Spec(R), S'=Spec(R') and X'=Spec(A') be a cartesian square of affine schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-base-change], with f:X\to S and g:S'\to S, and let K correspond to a complex M^\bullet of A-modules and K' to a complex N^\bullet of A'-modules in the quasi-coherent derived categories [def-pc-derived-category]. Let L(g')^*K\to K' be a map in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_{X'}), equivalently a morphism M^\bullet\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A'\to N^\bullet in D(A') via [lem-pc-affine-derived-pullback-tensor-tilde]. For a prime x' of A', let x be its image in A and let s' and s be their images in R' and R. If for every such x' and every i the canonical stalk map H^i(K_x\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_{S,s}}\mathcal O_{S',s'})\otimes_{\mathcal O_{X,x}\otimes_{\mathcal O_{S,s}}\mathcal O_{S',s'}}\mathcal O_{X',x'}\to H^i(K'_{x'}) is an isomorphism (equivalently, under the affine identifications, H^i(M^\bullet_x\otimes^L_{R_s}R'_{s'})\otimes_{A_x\otimes_{R_s}R'_{s'}}A'_{x'}\to H^i(N^\bullet_{x'})), then the induced derived pullback/direct-image comparison map [def-pc-derived-pullback, def-pc-derived-direct-image] M^\bullet\otimes^L_R R'\to M^\bullet\otimes^L_A A'\to N^\bullet is an isomorphism in D(R').

proof.text: Choose existing K-flat coordinates for phi from [def-pc-single-complex-base-change-stalk-condition]. For each degree i, apply [lem-pc-affine-base-change-cohomology-model] to obtain U,V,a, cohomology identifications, and additive localization identifications commuting with the stalk comparison.

For every maximal ideal J of A′, regard J as a prime. The hypothesis makes its stalk comparison bijective. Compose with the additive source equivalence to obtain bijectivity of lV after a_J; cancel the target additive equivalence to deduce bijectivity of a_J. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-linear-map-bijective-at-maximal-localizations] to a, so it is an isomorphism of A′-modules.

Restriction of scalars and tilde preserve this isomorphism. The commuting cohomology square identifies eU.hom followed by H^i(b) with F(a) followed by eV.hom, an isomorphism; cancel eU.hom. Thus H^i(b) is an isomorphism in every degree. The derived-category cohomology criterion DerivedCategory.isIso_iff [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] shows b is an isomorphism.
